60: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. 5313(a)(1): whether the 'for conviction of a felony' incarceration clock runs from the conviction (no contest plea and finding of guilt) or from sentencing. The court adopted the VA's reading that conviction is the trigger and rejected the veteran's sentencing-date reading.
we agree with the Veterans Court that the VA should use the date on which Mr. Mulder pleaded guilty and was convicted when calculating the date on which to reduce his benefits.
131: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 1151 causation: the court held that VA medical care need not proximately cause the disability (a lesser proximate-cause/remoteness standard applies), rejecting the government's reading that VA care must proximately cause the disability, and vacated and remanded.

To the extent the government argues and the Veterans Court concluded that VA medical care must proximately cause a claimant's disability, that is inconsistent with § 1151(a)(1)(B) and would render it a nullity.
292: Whether 38 C.F.R. 3.50(b)(1) and 38 U.S.C. 101(3) contain an exception allowing a divorced former spouse (abused spouse) to receive DIC as a surviving spouse; court held no exception exists and the VA's reading controls.

We discern no error in the Veterans Court's interpretation of §3.50(b)(1) as providing no exception to the requirement that the surviving spouse and veteran be married at the time of the veteran's death.
358: Whether 38 C.F.R. § 18b.73(b) governs appeals from denial of disability benefits; the court held it applies only to Title VI discrimination hearings and has no bearing on the appeal.
section 18b.73(b) has no bearing on Mr. Golemon's appeal from a denial of disability benefits
473: Interpretation and application of 38 C.F.R. § 4.130 (psychiatric disability rating criteria): the court held the Board and Veterans Court applied the rating regulation in accordance with law, including on whether specific findings on frequency, severity and duration were required.
We conclude that the Board and the Veterans Court applied 38 C.F.R. § 4.130 in accordance with law.
546: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 7453(e)(1) 'officially ordered or approved': court held Anderson line of cases (induced overtime is ordered or approved) governs, rejecting the government's express-directive reading.
We therefore hold that the Anderson line of cases' interpretation of the phrase "officially ordered or approved" in 5 U.S.C. § 5542 also governs that language where it appears in 38 U.S.C. § 7453.
553: Interpretation of VA rating code DC 5257: the court held the regulation is unambiguous and limited to impairments causing recurrent subluxation or lateral instability, rejecting the veteran's catch-all reading. This was stated as an alternative merits holding after the jurisdictional dismissal.

DC 5257 is unambiguous; by its plain language, it provides compensation for veterans suffering from impairments of the knee, other than those enumerated elsewhere in the relevant regulations, that cause the symptoms of recurrent subluxation or lateral instability.
856: Whether the Veterans Court erred by applying the 2006 version of 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c) rather than the 2002 version, which the government conceded was legal error requiring the court to apply the 2002 regulation on remand.
We remand for the Veterans Court to proceed in this case under the 2002 version of the regulation.
862: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 3.310(a) (and related §§ 3.156(b), 3.155(d)(2), 3.400(o)(2)): whether a claim for secondary service connection is part of the primary condition's claim. Court held it is not, adopting the VA's reading.
In short, § 3.310(a) does not make a claim for secondary service connection part of the primary service connection claim.
1050: Whether 38 U.S.C. § 7105 and VA regulations permit the VA to require NODs on a standard form identifying specific disagreements; held the statute is not exhaustive and the VA may add requirements.
we conclude 38 U.S.C. § 7105(b) is not exhaustive and does not restrict the VA's authority to fashion or articulate additional requirements claimants must satisfy in order to complete an NOD.
1221: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 4.71a, Diagnostic Code 5055, on whether it covers partial knee replacements; the court adopted the veteran's reading and declined to defer to the VA's interpretation under Auer.
Accordingly, we hold that Mr. Hudgens may be compensated under DC 5055 based on his partial knee replacement.
1329: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 19.9 (1995) and whether it applies to Board referrals as well as remands
We find persuasive Mr. Sucic's arguments that the referral by the Board raised procedural safeguards that the VA failed to implement.
1502: Whether a stand-alone 'abused widow' claim exists apart from surviving-spouse status under 38 U.S.C. § 101(3); court held the abuse allegation is only a factor in the continuous-cohabitation requirement, adopting the government's reading
We agree with the government. As an initial matter, we have jurisdiction over the purely legal question of whether there exists a stand-alone legal claim relating to Ms. Winsett's claim of abuse.
1506: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 3.304(f): the credible supporting evidence requirement requires evidence that the claimed in-service stressor occurred to the veteran, not merely that a stressor event occurred.
Accordingly, § 3.304(f) required Mr. Kays to submit credible evidence that he was involved in search and rescue activities and not simply that a civilian helicopter crash occurred.
1656: Interpretation of 1989 VA rating regulations: the regulations provided a single rating and maximum 10% rating for tinnitus, with no separate rating for each ear. Court upheld the VA reading.
We see no error in the interpretation made by the Veterans Court.
1788: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 5110 and 38 C.F.R. § 3.400(o): whether a statement of depression submitted while a colitis increase claim was pending can be a separate claim; the court rejected the veteran's reading of the statute and regulations.

We discern no reason why a submission raising a condition related to a primary condition cannot, itself, be deemed a "claim" for increased compensation within the meaning of § 5110 and the relevant regulations.
1848: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 3.317(a)(2)(ii): whether VA adjudicators may rely on a medical examiner's evaluation of whether a condition qualifies as a medically unexplained chronic multi-symptom illness (MUCMI) and whether a medical opinion limits future claims.
Therefore, we hold that VA adjudicators may rely on a medical examiner's evaluation of whether a veteran's condition qualifies as a MUCMI pursuant to § 3.317(a)(2)(ii).
1937: Interpretation of the implicit denial doctrine and the statutory notice requirement of 38 U.S.C. § 5104(b): the court held that implicit denial requires adjudication and notice of that adjudication, and that the 1993 decisions and 1994 letter could not implicitly deny the SMP claim.
Implicit denial requires adjudication and notice of that adjudication. Nothing less would satisfy the statute.
1947: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. 1154(b): whether combat-veteran lay evidence presumption applies to the nexus factor
we held in Davidson v. Shinseki that § 1154(b) only applies to the second Shedden factor: whether there was an in-service injury.
2203: Whether the implicit denial rule applies to formal and informal claims and to separately filed claims based on a distinct diagnosis, interpreting the pending-claim definition in 38 C.F.R. 3.160(c); court held it applies to both, rejecting the veteran's reading.
we conclude, like the court in Munro v. Shinseki, that the implicit denial rule applies to both formal and informal claims.
2289: Whether 10 U.S.C. § 1553 gives a veteran a clear legal right to expedited treatment of a PTSD-based benefits claim; the statute addresses only review of discharge or dismissal
2323: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 4.40 (functional loss) in relation to § 4.71a; whether § 4.40 provides a basis for a rating separate from § 4.71a. Court held § 4.40 must be read in light of § 4.71a and ratings are determined under § 4.71a criteria.
The answer is no; we affirm the judgment of the Veterans Court.
2433: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 7104(a): whether the Board may consider evidence not first considered by the Regional Office; court held the Veterans Court's reading of the statute was not erroneous.
We therefore reject Mr. Gainer's claim of legal error by the Veterans Court.
2502: Interpretation of EAJA fee statute (28 U.S.C. 2412(d)) regarding local vs. national CPI for cost-of-living adjustment; statute of general applicability, not a veterans benefit statute, so pro-veteran canon rejected
We therefore hold that the Veterans Court did not err in ruling that the local CPI approach represented the correct method of calculating the adjustment in Ms. Parrott's attorney's hourly rate.
2521: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 3.159(c)(3): the court held the regulation extends the VA's duty to assist to VA medical records regardless of relevance, reading the regulation in the veteran's favor.

We hold that § 3.159(c)(3) extends the VA's duty to assist to obtaining sufficiently identified VA medical records or records of examination or treatment at non-VA facilities authorized by VA, regardless of their relevance.
2558: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 1114(s)(1): whether additional disabilities must be rated under the combined ratings table (VA's reading) or by adding individual disability ratings (veteran's reading) for special monthly compensation eligibility.

we hold that § 1114(s)(1) unambiguously requires the veteran's additional disabilities be rated at least at sixty percent based upon the combined ratings table and not the addition of individual disability ratings as argued for by Mr. Gazelle.
2636: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 7105(d)(3) and 38 C.F.R. § 20.202: whether the March 1995 VA field examination report constituted a substantive appeal of the November 1994 SOC, including whether Rivera v. Shinseki and the liberal-reading rule and Douglas required review beyond the four corners of the document. The court adopted the VA's reading that the report did not reflect disagreement or a desire to appeal.

the Board properly found that the March 1995 report does not meet the criteria to be construed as a Substantive Appeal, as it does not reflect any disagreement with or desire to appeal the November 1994 SOC.
2877: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. statutes defining surviving spouse, child, and parent for DIC and death pension eligibility; court adopted VA's reading that payments are limited to the defined classes.
The statutes and regulations are unambiguous that DIC and death pensions are limited to the explicitly defined classes.
2888: Retroactive application of amended 38 C.F.R. § 20.1106 and § 3.10(f)(3) to bar a hypothetical-entitlement claim for enhanced DIC under 38 U.S.C. § 1311; court held the amended regulations may be applied retroactively (Princess Cruises factors), accepting VA's reading.

we find that, on balance, the Princess Cruises factors weigh in favor of applying the amendment to § 20.1106 and promulgation of § 3.10(f)(3) retroactively to bar Mrs. Moffitt's hypothetical entitlement claim.
2955: Whether 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)(1)'s term 'relevant' was properly interpreted; court held the term ambiguous and deferred to the Board's VA interpretation that the service records were not relevant.
The Board's interpretation does not strike us as either plainly erroneous or inconsistent with the VA's regulatory framework.
3026: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 3.303(a) (1964): whether the Board had to develop the record before deciding a service connection claim. Court agreed with the VA reading that the rule only requires full consideration of the evidence of record.
There is no requirement, implicit or otherwise, for the Board to develop the record before rendering a decision; it simply mandates full consideration of the evidence presented.
3128: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. 1521 and 101(29) 'period of war' definition; Lamm did not serve in a period of war as defined by Congress
there is no doubt that he did not serve in a "period of war" as Congress has defined that term.
3433: Interpretation of Diagnostic Code 7806 (38 C.F.R. § 4.118): whether topical corticosteroid treatment is 'systemic therapy' under the rating code. Court held the Veterans Court erred in reading the code as unambiguously treating any corticosteroid use as systemic therapy, adopting the Secretary's reading.

We agree with the Secretary that the Veterans Court incorrectly read DC 7806 as unambiguously elevating any form of corticosteroid treatment, including any degree of topical corticosteroid treatment, to the level of "systemic therapy."
3559: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. 20.1409(c) and 38 U.S.C. 7111: a veteran is limited to one CUE challenge per finally decided claim, so a final CUE decision is not itself subject to further CUE revision. The court adopted the VA's reading.
As we have previously made clear, however, a veteran is limited to one request for revision, or CUE challenge, for each disability claim finally decided by the board.
3633: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 5904(d): whether the VA's rating decision of January 31, 2008 constituted an award of past-due benefits on the veteran's claim despite the veteran's death, so that direct fee payment under § 5904 applies
We reject that statutory interpretation, concluding that § 5904 authorizes the fee payment in the circumstances of this case.
3634: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 20.609(h)(1)(iii): whether the regulation's cash-payment condition is satisfied where the award on the veteran's claim produced a cash payment to the accrued-benefits claimant from which the fee could be deducted
As a straightforward factual matter, the award to Mr. Finemore did "result[ ] in a cash payment . . . from which the fee may be deducted,"
3823: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 3.304(b) 'noted at entrance into service': whether only the DD 47 record of induction counts, or the SF 88 medical examination report also counts for the presumption of sound condition. Court held SF 88 counts, adopting the VA reading.

We conclude that the Veterans Court correctly interpreted 38 C.F.R. § 3.304(b)'s "noted at entrance into service" language to embrace conditions noted in an SF 88 medical report, not just in the DD 47 Record of Induction.
3929: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. 4.118 (2001) for the pre-2002 dermatophytosis rating: Green argued the Veterans Court required all four symptoms; the court held the Veterans Court did not misinterpret the regulation.
Accordingly, we conclude that the Veterans Court did not misinterpret 38 C.F.R. § 4.118 in its decision.
3930: Whether treatment records for unrelated conditions (38 C.F.R. 4.1, 4.2, 4.6) may be considered as pertinent evidence for a skin disability rating; the court held they may.
38 C.F.R. §§ 4.1, 4.2, and 4.6 do not narrow the universe of “pertinent” evidence to treatment records resulting from the examination of the particular disability-at-issue.
4014: Whether unlisted foot conditions may be rated by analogy under DC 5284 and whether the Board must consider DC 5284 for an unlisted condition despite listed conditions; the court held the Board erred in treating DC 5284 as foreclosed by pes planus.
We hold that they may and, indeed, such a rating by analogy must be considered by the Board for its determination to be complete.
4030: Meaning of 'disability' under 38 U.S.C. 1110: the court held pain alone, without a diagnosed underlying condition, can constitute a disability, reversing the Veterans Court's contrary legal interpretation.

We hold that the Veterans Court erred as a matter of law in holding that pain alone, without an accompanying diagnosis or identifiable condition, cannot constitute a 'disability' under § 1110, because pain in the absence of a presently-diagnosed condition can cause functional impairment.
4096: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 1116 'served in the Republic of Vietnam' includes territorial sea; veteran's reading adopted, overruling Haas
Because we hold that the unambiguous language of 38 U.S.C. § 1116 entitles Mr. Procopio to a presumption of service connection for his prostate cancer and diabetes mellitus, we reverse.
4135: Meaning of 38 U.S.C. 5101 and 5107 and related regulations on the required specificity of a formal claim; the court held the Veterans Court applied an incorrect legal test and that a formal claim must identify the condition at least at a high level of generality.
we hold that the Veterans Court formulated an incorrect legal test for determining if Mr. Sellers is entitled to an earlier effective date for his MDD condition.
4357: Interpretation of helpless child provision under 38 U.S.C. 101(4)(A) and 38 C.F.R. 3.57(a): appellant did not challenge the Veterans Court's interpretation, so no statutory interpretation question was decided
Mr. Ortegon does not identify any error in the Veterans Court's interpretation of § 3.57(a) or § 101(4)(A)
4363: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(b) and the Bell constructive-receipt doctrine: the court held VA-generated records need no actual knowledge by VA adjudicators to be constructively received post-decision, rejecting Turner's triggering-principle requirement, so the 1996 rating decision was not final.
We hold that the Veterans Court in Turner articulated an erroneous statement of the law when it failed to adequately address Bell and its progeny.
4433: Whether the Veterans Court applied the correct legal standard (TRAC factors) to an unreasonable-delay mandamus petition; court held the Veterans Court was required to consider TRAC factors
Here, it is enough to say that the Veterans Court should have considered the TRAC factors before dismissing Mrs. Mote's petition. Its failure to do so was legal error.
4664: Meaning of 38 U.S.C. § 5904(d)(1): whether 'past-due benefits awarded' refers to the total invalidated debt or only to benefits unpaid or owed to the veteran; court adopted VA's reading.
we agree with the VA and Veterans Court and find the language of § 5904—“past-due benefits awarded”—unambiguously refers to benefits unpaid or owed to the veteran.
5094: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 4.16(a) TDIU regulation: court held the Veterans Court applied rather than interpreted the regulation, so no reviewable legal interpretation was presented
Finally, examination of the Veterans Court's decision makes clear that it did not interpret § 4.16, but rather applied it to the facts of this case.
5146: Whether the Board must apply 38 C.F.R. 3.1(m)-(n), under which a service department line-of-duty or willful misconduct finding is binding on VA unless patently inconsistent with VA law; court held the Board erred by making its own findings despite service department findings in the record.
We conclude that the Board erred in simply making its own findings on the question of willful misconduct when there were service department findings before it.
5147: Whether a veteran's oral withdrawal of claims at a Board hearing is effective only if explicit, unambiguous, and made with full understanding of consequences (DeLisio standard), construed under 38 C.F.R. 20.204 and 3.103(c)(2); court adopted the veteran-favorable DeLisio standard and rejected the government's reading.
We believe DeLisio sets a reasonable standard for withdrawals at hearings as contemplated by 38 C.F.R. § 3.103(c)(2) and 38 C.F.R. § 20.204(b)(1), and adopt it as well.
5223: Interpretation of benefit statutes and regulations: whether VA regulation 38 C.F.R. § 3.12(d)(4) treating willful and persistent misconduct discharge as dishonorable is consistent with 38 U.S.C. § 5303 and § 101(2)
We hold that the regulation is consistent with, and authorized by, the statute.
5313: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 5110(g) limiting retroactivity of awards under liberalizing laws to one year before the claim and not before the effective date of the liberalizing law, adopting the VA's reading.

The result is that if the application for benefits is made after the date of the liberalizing law, the effective date is one year before the date of claim (but not before the date of the liberalizing law).
5709: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 5121(a) limiting which survivors may receive accrued benefits; the court applied the statute's limits against the son's position.
Pursuant to § 5121(a), only certain survivors of deceased veterans may be entitled to accrued benefits.
5753: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 5904(d)(3) (whether direct payment of attorney fees is mandatory or permissive) and 38 C.F.R. § 14.636(g)(3), (h)(4) filing requirement; court held the statute is permissive and VA need not directly pay fees when the regulation is not met
We agree with the Veterans Court that the plain language of § 5904(d)(3) cannot be read as mandatory.
5754: Validity of the 30-day regulatory filing requirement under 38 C.F.R. § 14.636(g)(3) and (h)(4) as within the Secretary's authority under Chevron, not arbitrary or contrary to statute

We agree with the Veterans Court that the 30-day filing requirement of 38 C.F.R. § 14.636(g)(3) and (h)(4), which is intended to allow VA to process direct-pay fee agreements as efficiently as possible, is eminently reasonable.
5877: Whether the CUE standard from Russell v. Principi, as adopted in Cook v. Principi under 38 U.S.C. § 5109A, should be abandoned or overruled; the court declined to revisit it and applied the Russell/Cook test as controlling law.
The reason is that this court has adopted the Russell test as controlling law.
5916: Whether the 48-month aggregate cap in 38 U.S.C. § 3695(a) precludes end-of-term extensions of Chapter 33 education benefits under 38 U.S.C. § 3031(f)(1); court held the cap applies only to the initial entitlement calculation, so it does not preclude end-of-term extensions.

Without a clear indication that Congress wished to impose the harsh consequence of automatic mid-semester benefits termination for multi-program beneficiaries, we hold that § 3695's aggregate cap applies only to the initial entitlement calculation.
5938: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 3.103(e) (1984 VA notice regulation): whether an explicit denial must state or clearly identify the claim being denied
we hold, as a matter of law, that to meet the notice requirements of § 3.103(e), an explicit denial must state, or clearly identify in some other manner, the claim(s) being denied.
5944: Whether 38 U.S.C. § 5304(a) prohibits concurrent receipt of a non-service-connected disability pension and service-connected disability compensation for the same period; court held the statute prohibits concurrent receipt, adopting the VA's reading.

We conclude that the Veterans Court correctly determined that section 5304 prohibited Mr. Harris from receiving both non-service-connected disability pension and service-connected disability compensation.
6046: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. 3.170 (1949)/3.343: the court held the regulation governing reductions of 100% ratings applies to a rating reset to 100% by CUE finding, rejecting the VA's Reizenstein-based reading
the regulation was applicable to Mr. Pirkl's situation in 1956, and a reduction, to be lawful, had to meet the regulation's requirements.
6088: Whether the Veterans Court applied the correct legal standard in reading the 1972 pre-2015 informal-claim regulation (38 C.F.R. § 3.155(a)) to Lacoste's 1972 application, i.e., whether the application must indicate an intent to seek benefits for the specific condition.
We see no legal error in the Veterans Court's decision, leaving for another day issues about the interpretation of the pre-2015 language of § 3.155(a) not raised here.
6126: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. 5307 and 101(31)/103(c): whether Ms. Batcher remained a veteran's 'spouse' for apportionment purposes after the 2005 judgment of separation; the court adopted VA's reading that she was a spouse from filing to divorce.
The Veterans Court correctly deemed Ms. Batcher eligible for apportionment as Mr. Batcher's spouse from the time she filed her claim to the date of the Divorce Decree.
6127: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. 101(24) 'active military, naval, or air service' and whether active duty for training qualifies under the ALS Rule; Bowers controls and the post-Bowers C-123 and Camp Lejeune rules do not alter it

We conclude, contrary to Mrs. Hansen-Sorensen's contention, that the C-123 and Camp Lejeune rules do not alter the Bowers statutory interpretation of the phrase "active military, naval, or air service" or the application of that phrase in the ALS Rule.
6195: Whether a NOD directed to the PTSD service-connection denial could also initiate appeal of the later 30% rating, and whether the 2015 standard-form regulation (38 C.F.R. § 20.201(a)(1)) requires VA Form 21-0958; court read the regulations as VA did.

we conclude that Mr. Hinton's NOD appealing the denial of service connection for his PTSD claim cannot also initiate appellate review of the 30% rating assigned to his service-connected psychiatric disorder.
6252: Application of 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c), the one-CUE-motion anti-multiplicity rule, to bar the due process CUE allegation; court adopted the VA's reading of the regulation.
We reject Mrs. Garcia's challenge to the Veterans Court's application of 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c) to bar her due process allegation of CUE.
6494: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 101(3) surviving spouse requirement: whether the domestic-abuse exception excuses proof of marriage at the time of death; court held marriage at death is required under Haynes, adopting the VA's reading.
Marriage at the time of death is a necessary predicate for a spousal death benefit claim, regardless of the reason for the divorce.
6577: Meaning of 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)(1)'s term 'relevant' (official service department records); court held the term has only one reasonable meaning, the VA's reading, and Auer deference does not apply.

To be relevant, a record must be relevant to the issue that was dispositive against the veteran in the VA adjudication of the claim sought to be reconsidered and, in that way, bear on the outcome of the case.
6632: Meaning of 38 C.F.R. § 3.155(a) (informal claims): the court held the Veterans Court applied too restrictive a reading of the regulation, requiring the filing itself to name the psychiatric disability, and adopted a more flexible, sympathetic-reading standard that lets specific referenced medical records identify the claimed benefit.
we conclude that the Veterans Court applied too restrictive a legal standard in reading her 2007 application. We vacate the Veterans Court's decision and remand for further proceedings.
6653: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 4.16(b): extraschedular TDIU requires inability to secure substantially gainful employment, not inability to work in the veteran's preferred position; the VA's reading prevails.
Whether the veteran can work in his or her preferred or current position is not the standard.
6657: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. 5121(a)(2)(B) 'the veteran's children' as limited to children meeting the section 101(4)(A) definition, excluding non-dependent adult children from accrued benefits eligibility

We hold that the term "[t]he veteran's children" in § 5121(a)(2)(B) is clearly and unambiguously governed by the definition of "child" in § 101(4)(A) and that Mr. Sucic's non-dependent, adult children are not eligible accrued benefits beneficiaries as "[t]he veteran's children."
6672: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c): whether the regulation's reconsideration of a spondylolisthesis claim based on new service records reopens the separate, secondary depression claim; court adopted VA's reading that it does not.

Pursuant to § 3.156(c), the Board's May 2012 determination directing the reconsideration of Mr. Brunette's spondylolisthesis claim does not, therefore, allow for introduction of evidence related to his secondary claim for depression.
6770: Interpretation of the M21 Manual herbicide-exposure provision: the manual requires credible evidence of perimeter duty, not corroborated evidence, so the veteran's reading prevails.
But the M21 Manual did not require Hudick to provide corroborated evidence. It required him to provide credible evidence.
6883: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. 3.156(c)(1): whether VA reconsidered the claim where service department records were associated before the 2008 reopening decision. Court upheld the Veterans Court's reading that VA's reconsideration requirement was satisfied and rejected the claimant's contrary reading.

Because the DVA considered Mr. Jones's claim in view of the records that Ms. Jones alleges should have been a part of the claimant's file from the outset, the DVA reconsidered the claim per 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)(1), as held by the Veterans Court.
6884: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. 3.156(c)(3): whether the award must be based on the newly associated records for both reopening and the award. Court held the Board and Veterans Court applied the correct standard, focusing on whether the award rested on the records, and rejected the claimant's reading.
As the Veterans Court ruled, the Board focused its analysis on whether the award was based on those records, and not on whether the decision to reopen the claim was based on those records.
6920: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 7107(b): whether a claimant previously given a Board hearing is entitled to another opportunity for a hearing after a Veterans Court remand.
We agree with Cook that § 7107(b) entitles him to an opportunity for an additional Board hearing in these circumstances.
6923: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 1115 'dependents' — whether dependency compensation extends to a grandchild not meeting the § 101(4)(A) definition of child; court held plain language limits dependents to spouses, children, and dependent parents, adopting VA's reading.
We agree with the Veterans Court that the plain language of § 1115 does not permit such an expansive definition.
6995: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. §§ 7266 and 7104(e): the Veterans Court's presumption-of-regularity rule for Board mailing of decisions and the standard for rebutting it, rejecting the veteran's proposed lower rebuttal standard.

Based on the statutory language, the Veterans Court correctly applied the presumption of regularity. It is not enough for Mrs. Sterling to show that she did not receive the mailing if the Board did not have any alternative address to send the decision.
6997: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. 7261(a)(2) unreasonable-delay standard: the Veterans Court applied the Costanza standard to mandamus petitions for unreasonable delay; the Federal Circuit adopted the D.C. Circuit TRAC factors as the proper standard and vacated and remanded for reconsideration under TRAC. Coded V01 as a question of statutory meaning; the court did not decide the merits of any individual delay.
we hold that the Veterans Court should look to the TRAC factors as guidance when evaluating mandamus petitions based on unreasonable delay in the VA's adjudication of benefits claims.
7062: Whether 38 U.S.C. § 1151(a) extends 'as if service-connected' treatment to chapter 37 home loan guaranty benefits; court held it does not, adopting VA's reading.
The plain language of § 1151(a) contradicts Ms. Burkhart's argument.
7063: Whether the incontestability provision in 38 U.S.C. § 3721 bars VA from contesting a COE issued before any loan was made; court held it applies only to the VA-lender relationship and only once a loan is issued, adopting VA's reading.
Section 3721 operates (1) as to the loan guaranty between VA and the lender and (2) only once a lender has actually issued a loan.
7147: Whether 38 C.F.R. § 3.816(c) governs the effective date for a Nehmer class member's increased rating rather than 38 U.S.C. § 5110(b)(3) and 38 C.F.R. § 3.400(o)(2); court held § 3.816(c) applies and § 5110(g) bars earlier retroactive benefits.
The effective date for a Nehmer class member is determined by 38 C.F.R. § 3.816(c) and not by 38 U.S.C. § 5110(b)(3) or 38 C.F.R. § 3.400(o)(2).
7148: Whether 38 C.F.R. § 17.33(a)(2) (prompt and appropriate treatment) bears on the effective date of VA benefits; court held it is a medical-treatment rule unrelated to effective dates.
Therefore, we agree with the Veterans Court that "§ 17.33(a)(2) is not related to the effective date of an award of VA benefits."
7277: Meaning of the 1946 schedule term 'defect' in 38 C.F.R.-era rating regulation: the court held 'defect' excludes degenerative conditions, favoring the veteran's reading.
We conclude that “defect” is properly construed as excluding degenerative conditions, and we do not understand the government to contend otherwise in this case.
7371: Whether VA reasonably treated the reconstructed roster, rather than the Form 23 affidavit, as the document issued by the service department under 38 C.F.R. 3.203(a)(1).
The VA's decision to treat the roster as the 'document issued by the service department,' 38 C.F.R. § 3.203(a)(1), was not arbitrary and capricious.
7393: Statutory interpretation of Section 2(c)(3) of the Blue Water Navy Vietnam Veterans Act: the Secretary had authority to stay pending claims from enactment (June 25, 2019) until the effective date (January 1, 2020); court held the VA reading controlled under Chevron step one.

Accordingly, we agree with the Secretary that the Act unambiguously authorizes him to stay the disability compensation claims described in § 2(c)(3)(B) of the Act, beginning on the date of the Act's enactment and ceasing on the Act's effective date.
7394: Whether the Secretary's stay authority under the Act extends to pending claims under 38 U.S.C. § 1116 as well as § 1116A; court held the Secretary properly interpreted the stay provision to reach § 1116 claims.
We conclude that the Secretary properly interpreted the stay provision to extend to § 1116 claims.
7450: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 5101(a)(1)(B): the court held the provision does not excuse a surviving spouse's failure to file a formal claim within one year of the veteran's death.

We simply hold that where, as here, the surviving spouse seeks survivorship benefits pursuant to § 5121, § 5101(a)(1)(B) does not excuse her failure to file a formal claim within one year after the veteran's death.
7453: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 5110(b)(3) and of VA regulation 38 C.F.R. § 3.400(o)(2): the court adopted VA's reading that an earlier effective date requires an increase in disability during the one year before the claim, and held the regulation does not conflict with federal law.
Accordingly, we hold that § 3.400(o)(2) is not in conflict with federal law.
7550: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 7261(b)(1) 'take due account' language: Veterans Court may not conduct independent non-deferential review of Board's application of benefit of the doubt rule and must apply clearly erroneous standard under § 7261(a)(4) and no de novo fact-finding under § 7261(c)

Based on the text of § 7261 and our precedent, the Veterans Court cannot conduct its own independent and non-deferential review of the facts to take due account of the Board's application of the benefit of the doubt rule.
7602: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 1.911(a): whether an overpayment of a veteran's attorney fee falls within the regulation's scope as participation in a VA benefit program. Court held it does, adopting the VA's reading.
Thus, the overpayment to Mr. Luckett of his attorney's fee falls within the scope of 38 C.F.R. § 1.911(a).
7610: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 5313: whether the statute requires VA to act during the incarceration period or permits a retroactive reduction of benefits for an already-ended incarceration period. Court adopted VA's reading.
we agree with the Veterans Court that 38 U.S.C. § 5313 authorizes VA to make a post-incarceration decision to reduce benefits retroactively for the specified period of incarceration.
7631: Whether service in the Wisconsin Army National Guard, including active duty for training without service-connected disability, satisfies the wartime service requirement of 38 U.S.C. § 1521(j) for non-service-connected death pension.

We affirm that, by statute, Mrs. Perry is not entitled to death pension benefits, and that the statutory requirement for wartime service for this purpose does not violate the constitutional right to equal protection.
7633: Whether the deceased obtained veteran status under 38 U.S.C. § 101(2) and 38 C.F.R. § 3.1705 so as to qualify for non-service-connected burial benefits.
On the undisputed facts, the Veterans Court's decision is in accordance with the statute and regulations, and is affirmed.
7651: Whether the Veterans Court has equitable authority absent an explicit statutory grant, and whether the 38 U.S.C. 5110(a)(1) claim-filing requirement is jurisdictional; the court held the Veterans Court has such authority and the requirement is not jurisdictional.
Accordingly, the Veterans Court erred in concluding it lacked equitable authority absent an express statutory grant.
7785: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. 3.12(c)(6): whether the compelling-circumstances exception applies to AWOL periods under 180 days. Court held the provision applies only to AWOL of at least 180 days, so the veteran's reading was rejected.
As the Veterans Court held long ago, the compelling-circumstances exception of that provision is not an exception to the 180-day precondition.
7786: Interpretation of the insanity exception in 38 C.F.R. 3.12(b) and 3.354(a): veteran argued knowing the nature of one's actions is the touchstone. Court found no error of law in the regulation's interpretation.
Mr. Stanton has identified no error in interpretation that affects his case.
7792: Interpretation of 'eligible for benefits' in § 101(e) of the Veterans Benefits Act of 2003: bound by Carroll, the court held the phrase refers to the possibility of receiving benefits, rejecting the argument that a spouse is ineligible to file until a presumption was adopted (alternative holding if jurisdiction existed).
There, we held that the phrase "eligible for benefits" refers to the possibility of receiving benefits and not entitlement to benefits.
7834: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 1724(a) 'furnish' phrase: whether it covers VA payment or reimbursement for non-VA treatment abroad; court adopted the VA reading

We conclude that the "furnish" phrase at issue covers what Mr. Van Dermark claims here—VA payment for a veteran's treatment (i.e., hospital care or medical services), whether payment is made to the treated veteran or to those to whom the veteran owes a debt for the treatment.
7835: Whether §§ 1728 and 1725 override the § 1724(a) prohibition on treatment abroad; court held they can be harmonized and do not override it
We also conclude that §§ 1728 and 1725 do not override the § 1724(a) prohibition.
7851: Whether 38 C.F.R. § 20.1000(c) (fraud-based reconsideration limited to allowances of benefits) is a reasonable Chevron gap-filling interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 7103, so the VA's reading controls.
the VA has discretion to enumerate the circumstances under which the Board will grant reconsideration.
7852: Whether § 20.1000 is contrary to law or arbitrary because it is not pro-claimant in every case; court held the regulation as a whole is consistent with the pro-claimant policy.
we must take care not to invalidate otherwise reasonable agency regulations simply because they do not provide for a pro-claimant outcome in every imaginable case.
7853: Whether the Veterans Court correctly read § 20.1000's three bases for reconsideration as exhaustive; court held the regulation authorizes reconsideration in only those three circumstances.
The regulation is clear on its face—§ 20.1000 authorizes reconsideration in only three specific circumstances
7862: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. 4.59 (painful motion rating): whether it requires a minimum 10 percent rating for any painful joint regardless of the applicable diagnostic code. Court adopted the Secretary's reading that 4.59 applies only in conjunction with the applicable diagnostic code.
For several reasons, those principles lead us to agree with the interpretation of section 4.59 that the Veterans Court adopted in Sowers and applied in this case.
7863: Statutory argument under 38 U.S.C. 1155 and 1114 that a veteran with a disability must receive a compensable rating of at least 10 percent. Court held the premise wrong, since statutes and regulations recognize noncompensable disabilities.
The premise of that argument is wrong.
7881: Court stated it disagreed with the claimant's argument that the Veterans Court misconstrued 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.321 and 3.324 by failing to combine the cyst with CTS and arthritis claims.

To the extent that Mr. Sorrell argues that the Veterans Court misconstrued 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.321 and 3.324 by failing to consider the compensability of his right wrist cyst in combination with his CTS and arthritis claims, see Appellant’s Br. 5–7, we disagree.
8015: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 3327(d)(2): whether the limit on Post-9/11 entitlement for veterans who switch unused Montgomery benefits applies to veterans with multiple periods of service; court held plain language applies, adopting VA's reading
Because we hold that the plain language of § 3327(d)(2) applies to veterans with multiple periods of service, we reverse.
8016: Whether the 48-month aggregate cap in 38 U.S.C. § 3695(a) displaces or limits the § 3327(d)(2) limit; court held § 3695 does not make § 3327(d)(2) inapplicable
Section 3695 does not state or imply that the plain language of 38 U.S.C. § 3327(d)(2) is inapplicable to veterans with multiple periods of service.
8039: Interpretation of the note in 38 C.F.R. 4.124a on combined nerve injuries: the court held the phrase refers only to service-connected injuries, so a combination of service-connected and non-service-connected nerve injuries does not trigger radicular group rating, adopting VA's reading without deference.
We hold that "combined nerve injuries" in the note refers to service-connected injuries, not to a combination of service-connected and non-service-connected injuries.
8112: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 7105(b)(2) ('claimant') and 38 C.F.R. § 3.665: the apportionment right belongs to the potential recipient, and the statutory term 'claimant' does not cover a veteran who files an apportionment claim on another's behalf, adopting the VA's reading.
The ordinary meaning of "claimant" under that statutory provision does not encompass any person who files a claim but, rather, refers to the person who would receive the benefit if granted
8158: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. 1725(c)(4)(D): whether a deductible is a similar payment to a copayment, so that reimbursement is barred. Court held deductibles are similar payments and excluded, adopting the VA's reading.
we conclude that the correct reading of the statute is one in which a deductible is a "similar payment" to a copayment, but coinsurance is not.
8159: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. 1725(c)(4)(D): whether coinsurance is a similar payment to a copayment. Court held coinsurance is not a similar payment and is not excluded from reimbursement, adopting the veteran's reading.
Rather, coinsurance is the very type of partial coverage that Congress did not wish to exclude from reimbursement.
8183: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 3.12(d)(1): whether an OTH discharge accepted in lieu of general court-martial is an 'undesirable discharge' barring benefits; court held regulation unambiguous and applies to OTH discharge, so the VA's reading prevails.

Accordingly, all the available evidence points to the same unambiguous reading of § 3.12(d)(1): Mr. Cranford's OTH discharge in lieu of trial by court-martial falls within the meaning of and is equivalent to an undesirable discharge.
8191: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. 3.156(c) automatic reopening on service department records, and whether the Board was required to assign an effective date under 3.156(c)(1)(iii); court adopted VA's reading
We agree with the VA's interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c).
8200: Meaning of 38 U.S.C. § 5904(c)(1): whether 38 C.F.R. § 14.636(c)(1)(i) may restrict attorneys' fees for § 5104C(b) supplemental claims; held contrary to the statute and invalidated, favoring the veterans' reading.
For these reasons, we hold that § 14.636(c)(1)(i) is contrary with the plain and ordinary meaning of § 5904(c)(1), and we thus invalidate that regulatory provision.
8201: Meaning of 38 U.S.C. § 5104C: whether 38 C.F.R. § 3.2500(b) may bar filing a supplemental claim while a federal court appeal is pending; held invalid as contrary to the statute's clear text, favoring the veterans' reading.
We therefore hold that § 3.2500(b) is invalid for contravening § 5104C's clear statutory text.
8265: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 3.114(a): whether the 2010 addition of § 3.304(f)(3) was a 'liberalizing' law or VA issue entitling the veteran to an earlier effective date
We conclude that the addition of § 3.304(f)(3) in 2010 was "liberalizing" under § 3.114(a).
8288: Whether the VA's denial of the rulemaking petition rested on a contrary or impermissible reading of the Agent Orange Act (38 U.S.C. § 1116) limiting presumptions to tactical herbicides; the court held the denial was not contrary to law.
The Agent Orange Act does not give presumptions to anyone other than those who "served in the Republic of Vietnam"—nor does it require the VA to do so.
8387: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. 105(a) and 1131 and 38 C.F.R. 3.1(n): the willful misconduct bar applies where the misconduct is the proximate (not necessarily direct) cause of the injury, rejecting the veteran's direct-cause reading.
The Veterans Court correctly interpreted the willful misconduct standard in 38 U.S.C. §§ 105(a) and 1131, and so we affirm its decision denying Mr. Carter service connection for his head injury.
8389: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 5103(a): whether the VA must wait until after a claim is received to provide evidentiary notice. The court held the current statute does not impose a post-application timing requirement, so the VA's reading prevails.
the current version of 38 U.S.C. § 5103(a) does not require the agency to wait to provide notice until after it receives a veteran's application.
8447: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. 3.156(c): the 2008 Board in effect conducted a reconsideration of the claim, and section 3.156(c) requires nothing more; the VA reading prevails.
As the Veterans Court explained, section 3.156(c) requires nothing more.
8448: Legal interpretation of 3.156(c): the 2010 JSRRC coordinator memorandum is not an official service department record, so it did not trigger reconsideration; the VA reading prevails.

The Veterans Court determined that, as a matter of law, an internal memorandum from a DVA employee commenting on evidence already of record does not constitute a service department record under section 3.156(c).
8470: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. 7104(d): the Board must address all regulations made potentially applicable by the assertions and issues raised in the record, not only favorable or relevant evidence. The court agreed with the veteran's reading.
We agree with Mr. Thomas and thus vacate the Veterans Court's decision and remand.
8484: Whether 38 U.S.C. § 5303(a) bars the veteran's benefits; court held section 5303(a) does not preclude benefits because the veteran was not convicted by court-martial and his AWOL periods did not run 180 days.
We agree with Mrs. Grounds to the limited extent that section 5303(a) does not preclude Mr. Grounds from obtaining VA benefits.
8485: Whether 38 C.F.R. § 3.12(d)(4) is a permissible additional bar to eligibility for benefits based on willful and persistent misconduct; court followed Garvey and held the regulation permissible and the Board did not err in applying it.
There we further held, expressly, that section 3.12(d)(4) is a permissible additional prohibition on eligibility for benefits.
8486: Whether the veteran was discharged under conditions other than dishonorable so as to be a 'veteran' under 38 U.S.C. § 101(2); court held the discharge was under dishonorable conditions under section 3.12(d)(4).

Mr. Grounds, however, was not discharged "under conditions other than dishonorable," because section 3.12(d)(4) provides that "[a] discharge or release because of . . . [w]illful and persistent misconduct" is a discharge under "dishonorable conditions."
8626: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 1503(a)(1): whether state unemployment compensation payments are excluded from annual income as 'donations from public or private relief or welfare organizations'; court held they are not donations, adopting the VA's reading.
we find that unemployment compensation payments are not "donations" within the meaning of 38 U.S.C. § 1503, and thus we affirm.
8673: Whether the Veterans Court applied the wrong legal standard by relying on Boggs rather than Clemons's lenient claim-scope rule in construing a pro se veteran's request to reopen; the court held Clemons applies to requests to reopen and affirmed on the Veterans Court's alternative Clemons holding.
In sum, the Clemons lenient-claim-scope rule applies to requests to reopen and Boggs does not require otherwise.
8685: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(b) (new and material evidence) and 38 C.F.R. § 20.3 (definitions of claim and benefit): court rejected the veteran's broad reading and adopted the VA's reading that separate primary and secondary claims are not the same claim for effective-date purposes.
We reject that broad reading of section 3.156(b).
8722: Interpretation of benefit statutes: whether the Veterans Court may make de novo findings of fact in applying prejudicial error review; court held §7261(b) does not permit de novo fact findings or resolving matters open to debate

we hold that § 7261(b)'s command that the Veterans Court "give due account of the rule of prejudicial error" does not give it the right to make de novo findings of fact or otherwise resolve matters that are open to debate.
8809: Interpretation of the Blue Water Navy Vietnam Veterans Act of 2019 and 38 U.S.C. § 1116A as to the offshore (12 nautical mile) scope of presumed Agent Orange exposure; court adopted the VA's reading.

we do not share MVA's view that the VA's interpretation of the Blue Water Navy Vietnam Veterans Act of 2019 unduly narrowed the presumption of exposure and service connection as applied to shipboard service.
8811: Alternative merits holding on the Airspace Rule: the exclusion of high-altitude missions from the Agent Orange presumption is consistent with the statute, so the VA's reading was upheld.
However, even if the time bar did not apply, we also agree with the Secretary on the merits.
8860: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 5313(c): whether 'incarcerated in a ... penal institution or correctional facility' covers commitment to a state mental hospital after a guilty-except-for-insanity judgment; court held it does not, so TDIU bar does not apply.

Because the Oregon State Hospital is not a "penal institution or correctional facility" under § 5313(c), we reverse the Veterans Court's decision that Mr. Philbrook was barred from receiving a TDIU rating as a matter of law.
8881: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(b): whether VA must explicitly state its new-and-material-evidence determination or may satisfy the regulation implicitly without magic words
we hold that the VA may fulfill its mandatory obligation under § 3.156(b) implicitly.
8887: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. §7105(b)(1): a notice of disagreement must be filed with the RO, so a January 2017 letter sent only to the Board cannot serve as an NOD as a matter of law.
Mr. Delano does not dispute the letter was not submitted to the RO, so, as a matter of law, it cannot serve as an NOD.
9047: Whether the term 'liquids' in DC 7203 is genuinely ambiguous; court vacated and remanded for reconsideration of any true ambiguity, finding the Veterans Court jumped too quickly to ambiguity.
We, thus, vacate and remand this matter for reconsideration of whether there is any true ambiguity in DC 7203.
9048: Whether the VA's interpretation of 'liquids' merits Auer deference; court held the VA's litigating position and withdrawn amendment did not reflect fair and considered judgment, so no deference is owed.
Under these circumstances, we owe no deference to the VA's interpretation of 'liquids.'
9049: Application of 38 C.F.R. § 4.7 'more nearly approximates' test; court held that without a definition of 'moderate' it is impossible to determine whether the condition more nearly approximates the 50% rating, a legally insufficient analysis.

Without any regulatory definition of '[m]oderate,' it is impossible to determine under 38 C.F.R. § 4.7 whether Mr. Roby's disability status more nearly approximates the criteria required for the 50% than the 30% rating of DC 7203.
9107: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. 1111 presumption of soundness and 1153 presumption of aggravation; court held Veterans Court correctly interpreted the statutes, requiring government to show both preexisting condition and lack of in-service aggravation by clear and unmistakable evidence
Because the Veterans Court correctly interpreted the relevant statutes in accordance with the statutory language and our precedent, we affirm.
9165: Whether 42 U.S.C. § 659 authorizes VA to withhold disability compensation for alimony when the veteran waived retired pay; court held § 659 and § 1408 work together and VA may garnish.

Accordingly, the Veterans Court correctly determined that § 659 authorizes the VA to withhold a portion of a veteran's VA disability compensation for alimony when the veteran has waived a portion of military retirement pay to receive disability compensation.
9174: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 3.307(b): whether the regulation requires a determination that the veteran had an acute diagnosis in 1978 before a disease can be treated as chronic; the court held it does not, adopting the VA's reading.
The plain meaning of the regulation is clear and permissive: diseases listed in Section 3.309(a), "even though diagnosed as acute," may still be accepted as chronic
9184: Chevron challenge to the VA's 'in need of personal care services' definition requiring in-person care; the court upheld the VA's reading as a permissible construction at step two.
The VA's interpretation of the statutory silence is a permissible construction of the statute.
9185: Chevron challenge to the VA's 'serious injury' definition requiring a 70 percent service-connected rating; the court upheld the VA's definition.
We cannot say the VA's definition of "serious injury" is an unreasonable policy choice.
9186: Chevron challenge to the VA's 'inability to perform an activity of daily living' definition requiring inability each time the ADL is completed; the court upheld the VA's reading.
To conclude, the VA's interpretation of "inability to perform one or more activities of daily living" is reasonable.
9187: Chevron challenge to the VA's 'need for supervision, protection, or instruction' definition requiring a personal-safety impairment and daily need; the court held the definition conflicts with the statute at step one and set it aside.
We, therefore, grant the petition on this ground.
9188: Chevron challenge to the VA's regulation limiting family caregiver benefits to residents of a State; the court upheld the residency requirement at both steps.
We cannot say the VA made an unreasonable policy choice limiting the family caregivers program to those caregivers who reside in the United States.
9189: Chevron challenge to the VA's monthly stipend rate tied to the GS scale; the court upheld the VA's gap-filling schedule.
The VA's use of the GS scale is a permissible construction of the statute.
9190: Chevron challenge to the 'unable to self-sustain in the community' definition used to set the full stipend tier; the court upheld the VA's two-tier definition.
We therefore deny the petition as to this ground.
9204: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. 3.309(a) 'psychoses' as a category of diseases rather than a single exemplary disease for the same-chronic-disease requirement under 3.303(b); court adopted the Secretary's reading.
We hold that "psychoses" as listed in § 3.309(a) must be interpreted as a category of diseases as a legal matter
9322: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 7107: whether the statute unambiguously requires the veteran's personal presence at a Board hearing for counsel to present witness testimony; court held it does not unambiguously so require, reading the statute as allowing representative participation.
we conclude that § 7107 does not unambiguously so require, we vacate and remand for further consideration of the statute and the agency's related regulations.
9337: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 3.312(c)(3): the court found no legal error in the Veterans Court's premise that the Robinson standard permits consideration of the regulation's second sentence, so the VA's reading controls.
We see no legal error in the Veterans Court's premise.
9376: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 3.321(b)(1): whether the Director of Compensation Service may consider an agency recommendation before deciding whether to approve an extra-schedular rating, in light of Thun v. Shinseki.
The plain language of the regulation does not prohibit the Director from considering an agency recommendation before making a decision regarding an extra-schedular rating.
9393: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 3.309(e): whether the herbicide presumption list excludes paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and hypertension. Court agreed with the VA reading.
Thus, the Veterans Court properly interpreted § 3.309(e) to exclude paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and hypertension.
9403: Whether the VA may interpret a §5904(d) fee agreement to determine whether it covers the claim that produced the past-due benefits, and so decline to pay fees from benefits on an excluded claim. The court held the VA correctly interpreted §5904(d) in declining to pay fees on a claim excluded from the agreement.
Our decision is only that the VA correctly interpreted § 5904(d) in declining to pay Mr. Viterna a fee out of past-due benefits on a claim excluded from his agreement with Ms. Pitts.
9438: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(b): whether the regulation requires VA to explicitly state that submitted evidence is new and material; court held an implicit determination suffices, adopting the VA's reading.

Following our precedent in Pickett, all that was required to satisfy § 3.156(b) was some indication that (1) the VA had determined that the May 1999 statement and May 1999 VA examination report were new and material, and (2) the VA considered that evidence as to her 1999 TDIU claim.
9633: Validity of 38 C.F.R. § 3.10(f)(3), which defines 'was entitled to receive' under 38 U.S.C. § 1311(a)(2); the court upheld the VA regulation against the hypothetical-entitlement challenge.
None of Ms. Hibbard's arguments undermine our previous holding, which recognized the possibility of an as-applied challenge to 38 C.F.R. § 3.10(f)(3)
9640: Interpretation of benefit statutes and regulations: whether the presumption of soundness in 38 U.S.C. § 1111 as understood at the time, and the 1970s/1977 version of 38 C.F.R. § 3.304(b), governs the CUE inquiry; court held the regulation in force at the time controls.

In other words, the VA does not commit clear and unmistakable error in a benefits claim decision when it faithfully applies a regulation as it existed at the time of decision, even if that regulation is later revised or invalidated.
9709: Whether 38 U.S.C. § 101(3) and 38 C.F.R. § 3.50(b)(1) contain an exception to the requirement that the surviving spouse be married to the veteran at death, for a divorce precipitated by the veteran's physical abuse; the court held there is no such exception, adopting the VA's reading.
Given the clear language of the statute and our binding precedent, we decline to disturb the Veterans Court's decision to deny Ms. Martin surviving-spouse status under 38 U.S.C. § 101(3).
9725: Whether the AMA required the claimant to use the AMA appeals system for a rating decision noticed after February 19, 2019, under the statute and regulations.
By its plain terms, the AMA specifies that if a claimant receives notice of a VA rating decision after February 19, 2019, he must file any challenge to that decision through the AMA appeals system.
9736: Interpretation of the note to 38 C.F.R. § 4.114, Diagnostic Code 7343: whether the mandatory VA examination and § 3.105(e) notice requirements apply to retroactively assigned 100% ratings. The court held they do not, adopting the VA's reading.
Because the Veterans Court properly interpreted 38 C.F.R. § 4.114, Diagnostic Code 7343, we affirm.
9800: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 5904(c)(1) (2012): meaning of 'the case' for fee eligibility; the Veterans Court's reading, consistent with Jackson, was upheld and the fee claim for the increased TBI schedular rating was held outside the case defined by the NOD.
we find the Veterans Court's interpretation consistent with our pre-2006 § 5904(c)(1) caselaw. Accordingly, we affirm.
9873: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 5304(c) and 38 C.F.R. § 3.654(b)(2): whether the statute speaks to the effective date for recommencement; court held statutory gap and upheld the VA regulation as reasonable gap-filling
Because we hold § 3.654(b)(2) reasonably fills a statutory gap, we affirm.
9934: Whether the AMA's enhanced §5104(b) notice requirements apply to a legacy claim decided by the Board after February 19, 2019; court held the legacy claim was not subject to the AMA notice requirements (VA's reading of the applicability provision).
We therefore agree with the Veterans Court that the Board was not required to comply with the enhanced notice requirements of amended § 5104(b).
9953: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 3.655(a)-(b): the court held that the claim for increase was properly denied under the plain language of the regulation, adopting the VA's reading over the claimant's argument that the claim should be rated on the evidence of record.
Thus, the Veterans Court correctly interpreted § 3.655 by its plain language when affirming the Board's denial of Mr. Gainer's claim.
10044: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 3033(a) and 38 C.F.R. § 21.7143(a): whether the duplication bar applies to Post-9/11 benefits paid in error and whether benefits for overlapping study periods count as concurrent assistance. Court adopted the VA's reading.
Because the Veterans Court properly interpreted the statute, we affirm.
10086: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 4.20: whether a veteran's unlisted condition must meet every criterion of the analogous diagnostic code (DC 7522) or only be closely related to it; court held the listed condition need only be closely related, not identical.
We hold that, when rating by analogy under § 4.20, the VA must adhere to the requirements of that regulation.
10087: Whether 38 U.S.C. § 501(a) authorizes the Secretary to adopt a conditional service-connection presumption for ALS, and whether the 90-day requirement contradicts §§ 101(2), 5303A and other statutes.

We agree with the Secretary that § 501(a) supplies the required statutory authority for the regulation and that § 3.318, as an exercise of the § 501(a) authority to adopt conditional presumptions of facts required by 38 U.S.C. § 1110, is not contrary to other statutory provisions cited by Mr. Snyder.
10123: Whether extra-schedular consideration under 38 C.F.R. 3.321(b)(1) and secondary service connection under 3.310(a) require a direct causal link between a secondary condition (ear pain) and the service-connected hearing loss; the court held direct causation is not required.
Direct causation is not required. Nothing in the regulation governing extra-schedular ratings provides otherwise.
10156: Meaning of 'Secretary' in 38 U.S.C. § 7261(b)(1): held to include the Secretary acting as the Board for final agency decisions, so the Veterans Court reviews the Board's benefit-of-the-doubt application (VA's reading).
we hold that the term “Secretary” in § 7261(b)(1) includes the Secretary acting in his capacity as the Board for the purpose of making a final agency decision.
10157: Scope of review under § 7261(b): the veteran's argument for de novo, non-deferential review was rejected; the Veterans Court properly reviewed for clear error while taking due account of the Board's application (VA's reading).
Accordingly, we held that the Veterans Court properly reviewed the Board’s factual determination for clear error while taking due account of the Board’s application of the benefit of the doubt rule.
10206: Meaning of 'resided at Camp Lejeune' under 38 U.S.C. § 1787(a): the court held the plain meaning covers only those who lived on base, rejecting constructive residence based on time spent there and statutory purpose arguments.
We agree with the Veterans Court that "resided at Camp Lejeune" has a plain meaning that includes only those who lived on base.
10287: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 4324 as not providing a right of action against OPM for differential pay owed by another agency
Section 4324 does not permit him to recover differential pay owed by DHS from OPM.
10318: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 7104(a) 'one review on appeal' and the VA's handling of the pending appeal through 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(b) and the RO's December 2012 decision; court rejected the veteran's reading.
Mr. Silva is incorrect, however, when he asserts that he was deprived of that appeal.
10320: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 5107(b) 'approximate balance': the court held that the benefit-of-the-doubt rule covers evidence that is nearly equal, not only exact equipoise, and rejected Lynch's narrower equipoise reading of Ortiz.

Under § 5107(b) and Ortiz, a claimant is to receive the benefit of the doubt when there is an "approximate balance" of positive and negative evidence, which Ortiz interpreted as "nearly equal" evidence.
10324: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 3.344(c): majority held the parenthetical '(5 years or more)' is definitional, so the stability procedures of (a) and (b) apply only to ratings unchanged for five years or more (VA's reading).
we conclude that § 3.344(c) makes the procedures of §§ 3.344(a) and (b) applicable only to disability ratings which have continued at the same level for five years or more.
10329: Interpretation of the VA General Rating Formula for spine disabilities in 38 C.F.R. § 4.71a: whether the VA must rate the thoracolumbar spine as a unit, so that a separate thoracic-only rating is not permitted.
We reject that interpretation and hold the plain language of the regulation requires that the VA treat the thoracolumbar spine as a unit when applying the General Rating Formula.
10342: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 1110 and 38 C.F.R. § 3.303(c): a Chiari network condition is a congenital defect, not a disease, so it is excluded from service connection.
On the statutory definition of eligibility for the presumption of service connection, and the undisputed medical facts, there is no basis for departing from the decision of the Veterans Court.
10367: Whether 38 C.F.R. §3.156(b) controls the effective date of a secondary service-connected disability; court held it does not.
First, we agree with the Veterans Court that § 3.156(b) does not control the effective date of Mr. Jordan's secondary service-connected condition.
10429: Whether the March 2015 submission qualified for accrued benefits under 38 U.S.C. 5121 as an intent to file; court vacated and remanded without deciding the legal question
We vacate the Veterans Court's decision regarding accrued benefits, and we remand for further proceedings.
10430: Whether the 2015 intent-to-file regulations governing claims filed after March 24, 2015 applied to the March 2015 submission received March 26, 2015; court adopted VA's reading

We see no legal error in the Veterans Court's first conclusion—that VA regulations effective March 24, 2015, govern a submission received by VA on March 26, 2015, even if the submission was allegedly mailed before that date.
10431: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. 3.1706 regarding burial benefits for a veteran allegedly turned away from a VA facility; court adopted VA's narrow reading
Mrs. Kriner's reading does not fit the regulation. Thus, we affirm the court's determination that Mrs. Kriner was not entitled to burial benefits.
10479: Interpretation of 10 U.S.C. 1174(h)(2) exception to SSB recoupment: whether the later-period-of-active-duty exception applies; court adopted VA's reading
The statutory language is clear that the exception applies only when the disability itself was incurred during a later period of active duty.
10510: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 5107(b) and 38 C.F.R. § 3.102: the court rejected Lynch's argument that Ortiz requires equipoise of the evidence, holding that approximate balance means nearly equal evidence, and affirmed the Veterans Court under that reading.
Ortiz explicitly gives force to the modifier "approximate" as used in 38 U.S.C. § 5107(b).
10635: Meaning of 38 U.S.C. § 7261(b)(1)'s requirement that the Veterans Court 'take due account' of the Secretary's application of the benefit-of-the-doubt rule; court held it requires no review beyond clear-error review and no sua sponte review.

the statutory command that the Veterans Court "take due account" of the benefit of the doubt rule does not require the Veterans Court to conduct any review of the benefit of the doubt issue beyond the clear error review required by § 7261
10704: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 5121A: whether a substituted survivor may raise a clear and unmistakable error (CUE) allegation that the deceased veteran never raised before death
Because we find that the Veterans Court did not misinterpret 38 U.S.C. § 5121A by denying a substituted claimant from raising a CUE allegation never raised by the deceased veteran, we affirm.
10777: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 5904 and 38 C.F.R. § 14.636(c)(2): whether attorney fees for services before a Board decision are limited to cases where the NOD was filed on or after June 20, 2007. Court held the statute's effective-date provision in the Statutes at Large limits fees, upholding VA's reading.

The text of the relevant portion of the Act as it appears in the Statutes at Large plainly limits attorney's fees for services provided prior to a final Board decision to cases in which an NOD was filed on or after June 20, 2007.
10797: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 1151 (VA medical care injury compensation): court held the Veterans Court correctly applied the statutory prerequisites and rejected the veteran's argument that the Secretary's reading was too narrow.
10899: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 1110: the court held that 'resulting from' requires only but-for causation, so compensation extends to a service-connected disease that impedes treatment of a non-service-connected disability. The court also held 38 C.F.R. § 3.310(b) unlawful to the extent it rejected this theory.
Put together, § 1110 plainly requires compensation when a service-connected disease or injury is a but-for cause of a present-day disability.
10921: Meaning of 38 U.S.C. § 1720G(c)(1) (medical determination language) and whether it bars Board and judicial review of all Caregiver Program decisions; held to bar review only of decisions on furnishing assistance or support, adopting the veterans' reading.
For the reasons set forth below, we hold § 1720G(c)(1) only bars judicial review of Caregiver Program decisions on the furnishing of assistance or support.
10956: Construction of 38 C.F.R. § 4.14 (anti-pyramiding): the court held the Veterans Court properly construed the regulation to bar compensating the same symptomatology twice under the diabetes rating, adopting the VA's reading.
Accordingly, we conclude that the Veterans Court properly construed § 4.14 to affirm the Board.
10958: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 3327(d)(2) and the 48-month aggregate cap under the GI Bill: whether a veteran with multiple qualifying periods of service is limited to unused Montgomery entitlement or may receive full Post-9/11 benefits subject to the 48-month cap.
The Veterans Court correctly held that each period of service earns education benefits, subject to its cap of 48 aggregate months of benefits.
10999: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c): whether an earlier effective date requires that the award be based at least in part on newly received service department records; court held both pre- and post-2006 versions require that the award be based in part on the new records, rejecting the veteran's reading.
Both versions of § 3.156(c) require that the award of benefits be based at least in part on the new service department records to qualify for an earlier effective date.
11029: Interpretation of DC 5055 (knee replacement rating). The court held the VA's Knee Replacement Guidance interpretation arbitrary and capricious, denied Auer deference under Hudgens, and applied the pro-veteran canon to adopt the veteran's reading.
For these reasons, we conclude that the Secretary's interpretation of DC 5055 is arbitrary and capricious and vacate the Knee Replacement Guidance.
11133: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.125(a) and 4.130: whether a DSM-5 diagnosis is required before a mental condition can be rated for service connection. Court adopted the VA's reading.
Because we agree with the Veterans Court that 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.125(a) and 4.130 require a DSM–5 diagnosis as a precondition to compensate a mental condition, we affirm.
11275: Whether 38 U.S.C. § 3562 bars additional compensation under § 1115 for a child receiving Chapter 35 DEA benefits, and whether the bar is permanent; court adopted the VA's reading following Wright v. Collins.
In Wright we held that the VA could plainly do so.
11279: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 4.59 (whether it applies to non-arthritis painful motion as of 2004); court declined to conclusively interpret it but held plain language did not undebatably apply to non-arthritic conditions
our decision is limited to the conclusion that § 4.59, on its face, did not undebatably apply to non-arthritic conditions.
11289: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 1114(s): whether 'a service-connected disability rated as total' can be satisfied by multiple disabilities whose combined ratings yield a total TDIU rating. Court adopted the VA's reading that only a single disability rated as total qualifies.

the plain language of § 1114(s) establishes that Congress did not intend for multiple disabilities with ratings combining to a disability rated as total to qualify as 'a service-connected disability rated as total.'
11290: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 4.16(a)'s 'one disability' clause: whether disabilities grouped as one disability under § 4.16(a) also count as a single disability rated as total for § 1114(s). Court held the § 4.16(a) grouping is limited to TDIU eligibility.

Thus, even if multiple service-connected disabilities are considered 'one disability' under § 4.16(a), that fact alone does not demonstrate 'a service-connected disability rated as total' for the purposes of § 1114(s).
11321: Whether the Veterans Court and Board could rely on the Federal Rules of Evidence principle that people seeking medical care have great incentive to tell the truth in giving greater probative weight to medical-treatment statements; court held no legal error.
We therefore see no error in the Board's reliance on a principle supported by the Federal Rules of Evidence that "when people need medical care, they have great incentive to tell the truth."
11547: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. 36.4406(c): whether the one-year filing deadline for SAH reimbursement requests by an eligible individual's estate applies, adopting the VA's plain-meaning reading.

We decline to adopt an interpretation of § 36.4406(c) that would render the explicit one-year filing deadline inapplicable because such an interpretation is contrary to the plain language of the regulation.
11594: Interpretation of the PACT Act: direct service-connection claims for hypertension were preserved under PACT Act § 407 and are separate from presumptive PACT Act claims, adopting the veteran's reading.
Such direct service-connection claims were explicitly preserved under the PACT Act.
11655: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 3.105(d) and § 3.105(a)(1) CUE standard for severing service connection; court held the VA's reading was correct and the Veterans Court did not err
Because the Veterans Court did not err in its interpretation of the applicable regulation, we affirm.
11670: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 3.350(f)(3): whether the SMC intermediate-rate provision permits more than one increase. The court held it unambiguously allows multiple intermediate-rate SMC increases, subject to the statutory cap, which is the veteran's reading.
As we explain below, § 3.350(f)(3) does not limit how many SMC increases can be provided; instead, it is a mandatory entitlement that can apply multiple times, subject to a statutory cap.
11738: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(b): whether the VA may satisfy its obligation to treat new and material evidence as filed in connection with a pending claim by issuing a Statement of the Case. The court held the Veterans Court correctly interpreted the regulation, so the VA's reading prevailed.
Because the Veterans Court correctly interpreted § 3.156(b), we affirm the Veterans Court's decision.
11865: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 5904(c)(1) and the § 101(h) effective-date provision of the 2006 Act: which version of the attorney fee statute applies to fees on the non-SMC PTSD award. The court held the Veterans Court applied an incorrect legal standard and that the post-Act version applies, so the veteran's reading prevails.

We now conclude that the Veterans Court relied on an incorrect legal standard in determining which version of § 5904(c)(1) applies, and we also conclude that the post-Act version is the applicable one.
11991: Interpretation of 38 U.S.C. § 7113(c): whether a veteran's NOD that refers to evidence already in the Board's possession satisfies the statutory requirement that evidence be submitted with the NOD. Court held the veteran's reading controls and reversed the Veterans Court.
we determine that Mr. Cash's February 2022 evidence qualifies as evidence submitted with Mr. Cash's NOD under 38 U.S.C. § 7113(c)(2)(A).
12006: Interpretation of 38 C.F.R. § 3.310(a): whether secondary service connection requires a causal link between the secondary condition and an underlying service-connected primary condition, rather than the in-service injury. Court adopted the VA's reading.
we hold that a veteran must demonstrate a causal relationship between a secondary condition and an underlying primary condition to succeed under a secondary service connection theory.
12258: Interpretation of the presumption of soundness (38 U.S.C. § 1111) and the claimed 'sympathetic reading' and 'trauma requirement' legal standards; Court held the presumption was not triggered and rejected the trauma-element reading, adopting VA's reading.
In short, the presumption of soundness is triggered by a veteran's entrance examination, not by an alleged bifurcation of a veteran's claims, as argued by Mrs. Williams.
12274: Whether the Veterans Court applied the correct legal standard in holding that Manzanares controls and that secondary-condition claims take the normal § 3.400 effective-date rules rather than the primary claim's date under § 3.156(b).
